title: Second look at N-005: the fragment and its label are as described, but the likeness to f35v is only in general form and the anchor names nothing, so it cannot serve as a pairing
statement: What I checked on the two Yale scans named in the anchor (the f89r2 crop 6280,145,1370,760 on canvas 1006233, and f35v on canvas 1006143). The description of the fragment holds: a broad green crown with a shallowly scalloped outline, carried on four or five pale stalks that converge on a rounded pale-brown base from which thick roots run out sideways, and one label line under the right half of the crown, to the right of the stalks. On f35v there is a green crown at the top of a bundle of straight stalks as well. The likeness stops at that general form. The f35v crown is made of separate leaves with deep rounded lobes and open sinuses, and two more such leaves are drawn lower on the plant; the fragment's crown is a single mass with a wavy edge and no leaf drawn separately. The f35v plant has thin stems twining round the main stalks and many clusters of round blue-green fruit, a few of them red; the fragment has neither, as the proposer says. The f35v root is red-brown, long and many-fingered; the fragment's base is a pale bulb with a few thick arms. So the two drawings share a crown-on-stalks outline that many plants in the manuscript could be said to share, and differ in leaf form, fruit, climbing stems and root. Why this is a dissent and not an agreement. An agreeing second look would mark the anchor confirmed, and a confirmed anchor is meant to be a pairing of a word with a thing whose name is known. This one lists no name, and its own statement says the crown cannot tell oak from ivy from a conventional leaf form. From the pinned ZL transliteration: the label as written occurs once in the manuscript, at this locus; its first part occurs nowhere else as a word; its second part is a common word (108 times on 62 pages) and does not occur among the 91 words of f35v. So the text gives no sign that the label and the f35v page are about the same plant either. I agree with the proposer's facts and with the word UNCERTAIN; I dissent from recording it as an anchor. It would be better kept as an observation for the picture-text tests (same object drawn twice, do the labels agree), where the answer here is that f35v has no label to compare. Not checked: the published comparisons by Zandbergen and Vatne and the BnF image; I did not open them and take no view on the ivy or oak identification of f35v.
sources: Zandbergen-Landini transliteration ZL 3b (pinned data/raw/ZL3b-n.txt): locus f89r2.4; word counts over all loci and over f35v
